summary.intent: Fix Google OAuth login in a Tauri desktop app (cipher-box) that was returning Error 400 (invalid_request) because Tauri's `tauri://localhost` scheme is rejected as a redirect URI by Google OAuth. After the fix, address PR review comments raised by Copilot.
summary.outcome: Implemented a temporary localhost HTTP server in Rust (`start_oauth_server` Tauri command) to receive the OAuth callback on `http://localhost:{port}/callback`, rewrote `getGoogleCredential()` in TypeScript to use it, fixed a Tauri capability permission gap blocking event listening, fixed an HTTP body-parsing bug in the Rust server, and addressed 5 of 6 Copilot review comments (nonce validation, scoped event names, absolute timeout deadline, popup cleanup counter, fail-fast port binding). Branch pushed as `fix/google-oauth-tauri-redirect` and PR #459 opened.

repo: cipher-box is a Tauri v2 desktop app in a pnpm monorepo; desktop app is run with `pnpm --filter desktop dev`
Tauri capabilities are declared in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` and must explicitly list permissions like `core:event:default` for webview APIs such as `listen()`
Google OAuth client ID is `164556913424-uif44is1apnl7rqc9a2ac7vn8u9dq0ee`; preferred callback ports to pre-register in Google Cloud Console are 14200, 14201, 14202
The `rand` crate in use is v0.8, which uses `thread_rng().gen::<u64>()` not the newer `rand::random()` API
An unrelated `cipherbox-fuse` version bump was present in `Cargo.lock` and had to be discarded before committing the OAuth fix

code.finding: `getGoogleCredential()` was building the redirect URI from `window.location.origin`, which resolves to `tauri://localhost` in production Tauri builds — rejected by Google OAuth. Fixed to call `start_oauth_server` and use `http://localhost:{port}/callback`.
Single `read()` call on the TCP stream failed to capture the full POST body when headers and body arrived in separate TCP segments. Fixed by reading until Content-Length is satisfied.

Timeout was being reset on every new connection rather than using an absolute deadline. Also, `oauth-callback` event name was global (collision risk); fixed to use a per-session scoped name returned by the server. Nonce added to POST payload and validated server-side. Popup cleanup loop was hardcoded to 0..99 instead of using the actual connection counter.
Missing `core:event:default` permission caused `Failed to start OAuth flow: event.listen not allowed` in the webview. Required for `@tauri-apps/api/event` listen/emit APIs.

workflow: Tauri v2 requires explicit capability grants per webview API; adding a Rust command is not enough if the frontend also needs event APIs

`GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable takes priority over `gh auth login` keyring credentials and cannot be overridden with `unset` in the Bash tool session — use `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh ...` as a workaround
Rust TCP servers doing a single `stream.read()` are unreliable for HTTP POST bodies; always read until Content-Length is satisfied
When using `rand` 0.8, verify API with `cargo metadata` before assuming the latest `rand::random()` API is available

friction: `git pull` failed immediately due to divergent branches with no reconciliation strategy configured — required manual `git fetch` + status check before proceeding
Dev server (`pnpm --filter desktop dev`) was launched three times in background before the app appeared in the macOS taskbar, with no clear signal it had actually started

`gh auth login` silently had no effect because `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var was injected at the shell environment level and could not be unset within the Bash tool session; required `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN` workaround
First OAuth attempt failed with `Failed to start OAuth flow: event.listen not allowed` — missing Tauri capability not caught at development time
Second OAuth attempt failed with `Failed to parse callback data` — single-read HTTP body parsing bug not caught before testing
`rand` 0.8 API mismatch caused a compile error after using newer `rand::random::<u64>()` syntax
open_items: Add `http://localhost:14200/callback`, `http://localhost:14201/callback`, and `http://localhost:14202/callback` as authorized redirect URIs in Google Cloud Console before the PR can be tested in production builds

Copilot comment #5 (`core:event:default` capability scoped to `windows: ["*"]` being too broad) was marked not applicable — worth revisiting if the app grows to multiple window types with different trust levels
The `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var injection issue has no permanent fix applied; may block future `gh` usage from the assistant
Release build testing of the OAuth flow has not been done — only verified on `dev` build
